paper_reference: Microsoft Research, From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization.
installation_command: git clone https://github.com/microsoft/graphrag.git external/graphrag && git -C external/graphrag checkout 14a00ad88fc33cf2b52f4f113f25807556f8e25e && python -m venv external/envs/graphrag && external/envs/graphrag/bin/pip install graphrag
isolation: Use a dedicated virtual environment under external/envs/graphrag or a container. Microsoft GraphRAG supports Python 3.10-3.12; this project targets a different runtime.
model_retriever_requirements: Official Microsoft GraphRAG index built outside version-controlled processed outputs.
Global-search configuration routed through Ollama or another local OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
A JSON-stdin runner wrapper that invokes global search at the pinned commit.

expected_output_mapping.stdin: JSON object with baseline_id, comparison_mode, session_id, query, target_time, evidence, budgets, and native_config.
expected_output_mapping.stdout: JSON object. Required: answer or final_answer. Optional: predicted_state/state, confidence, predicted_hypothesis_id, citation_supported, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd.
expected_output_mapping.native: Wrapper should call the official global search pipeline over a prebuilt GraphRAG index.
expected_output_mapping.controlled: Not listed as supported because global community summaries are not generally equivalent to common chunk evidence.

readiness_notes: Global search is native-only. Local-model support uses the upstream LiteLLM/proxy path and requires reliable structured JSON output.

state_support.abstain: unsupported unless the wrapper maps an official no-answer signal
state_support.unknown: evaluator_derived when no native state is emitted
